images.seen: Cliopatria draws only one Egypt outline; the compiled map gave the Twenty-first Dynasty the whole outline incl. Western Desert, Red Sea and Matruh with the priests' vassal tint a thin Nile strip, and a Kush strip cut by Egyptian cells south of the cataract; both patched

Cliopatria has nothing here; Kuru and Panchala (smaller) sit inside the Painted Grey Ware area, Sindhu-Sauvira is Sind plus a Multan disc; stand-in shapes but nothing contradicts the pages, fine as drawn

Cliopatria draws one Zhou shape; compiled carves the fiefs out of it (Zhou vassal tints for Song, Cao, Chen, Cai, Chu); Chu has an unowned hole round Jingmen/Xiangyang and Zeng owns 1 of its 52 disc cells (Chu holds the rest); fiefs fine, Zeng/Chu reported
Carchemish's disc covered Bit Adini's capital area and left Bit Adini a thin crescent south of it; patched with a ruling, redrawn fine
Israel/Judah split drawn with Philistia, Ammon, Moab, Edom, Aram-Damascus independent; the Samaria hills (about 6 cells round Shechem and Samaria) were unowned inside Israel; patched, now Israel's
Delta direct for the 21st Dynasty, priests' Nile valley as vassal tint, Kush keeps the land south of the first cataract; no desert outline
22nd Dynasty is Delta plus the Nile valley strip; Levant, Syria and Assyria heartland look as the pages describe; Neo-Assyrian Empire is a small heartland shape

issues.what: Twenty-first Dynasty keyframe new-kingdom-of-egypt_-1000 drew Cliopatria's whole Egypt outline: snap of +759 cells (New Valley 525, Red Sea 180, Matruh 48) the ledger does not explain; page: pharaohs 'mostly active only in Lower Egypt, which they controlled', priests ruled Middle and Upper Egypt 'in all but name'

Twenty-second Dynasty keyframe twenty-second-dynasty-of-egypt_-943 drew the same outline (+759 cells, 46 Giza cells missing); page names no land beyond Bubastis and Tanis; now the ledger's Delta plus the priests' Nile valley and Fayyum, held to -901

Judah's founding region 'Judea' reached the Samaria hills (to 32.46 N) and its keyframe then dropped those cells, leaving 6 cells round Shechem and Samaria owned by nobody (snap of 11 cells); the cells outside Judah's frontier and outside the contested Benjamin band go back to Israel

bit-adini / carchemish size-rule conflict (96 cell-years): Carchemish's 90 and 60 km discs took Bit Adini's capital land from -975; page puts Bit Adini in the Euphrates bend south of Carchemish with its capital at Til Barsip; south of Carchemish's latitude now Bit Adini's (approximate line)

high-priests-of-amun-at-thebes / kingdom-of-kush at Aswan (84 cell-years): the priests' Nile Valley region reaches the Sudan border and won 42 cells south of the first cataract by the size rule, cutting a strip of Egypt through Kush; page gives the first cataract at Elephantine as the traditional border; Kush now wins (the succession rule then keeps them Kush's for the 22nd Dynasty)

elam keyframe elam_-1000 removes 285 cells (Khuzestan 126, Bushehr 58, Fars 47 ...) with no ledger event; the Elam page only says power waned, 'Elam disappears into obscurity for more than three centuries' and 'Anshan was still at least partially Elamite' (so a Susa-only shape may be too narrow); no extent is given, so no event or override written

assyria assyria_-1000 snap of 1709 cells and zhou-dynasty zhou-dynasty_-1000 snap in the 1 Nov packet; both vanish in a trial that includes the m1100-m1001 patch (assyria_-1100 cut to -1056, wey_-1040 widened)

kuru-kingdom / painted-grey-ware-culture / panchala-kingdom conflicts (365 cell-years at -1000): the two kingdoms (smaller) win inside the culture area, which fills the rest; Zhou against its fiefs (lai, ju, pi, xing, liu-lu-an, ji-shandong, hu-luohe, sui-ningyang, xi, eastern-guo, jiang-*, kuai, wu) and sam-al, kammanu, philistia, babylonia/elam small-state wins likewise
kingdom-of-judah / philistia 11 cells at -930 won by Philistia: Judah's western edge is Gezer per the page and the drawn border sits at about 35.0 E; small, no change

patch_check: all applied (--check-patch: 5 of 5 ok; --trial: 5 applied; rulings/0 settled 55 cell-years, rulings/1 settled 42; keyframe snaps 7 -> 3: elam, carchemish_-975 (now 20 added, 21 kept by Bit Adini), kingdom-of-israel_-930 (removed 5, no visible change))
problems: zeng: its 60 km Suizhou disc (52 cells) is held by Chu from -1030 (chu_-1030, chu_-750 and chu_-700 cut circles round Jingmen, Xiangyang, Shiyan and E but not Zeng's disc), so Zeng owns 1 cell throughout -1000..-901; no conflict is recorded and a ruling acts only where claims meet, so I could not patch it inside this window. Suggested: the m1100-m1001 agent or the orchestrator adds the Zeng disc ({lon 113.38, lat 31.69, km 60}) to the minus lists of those three Chu keyframes (Zeng page 'territory in the area around Suizhou'; the Chu page 'original area (modern Hubei)'). Not opened by me.
chu: the -1030 and -750 keyframes leave an unowned hole of about 15 cells round Jingmen/Xiangyang inside Chu (the cut-out circles of Hubei fiefs, owned by nobody); deliberate in the dossier, left.

seam at -900: my twenty-second-dynasty keyframe override ends at -901; the same dossier's keyframe new-kingdom-of-egypt_-900 (starts -900, window m0900-m0801) draws the whole Egypt outline again, so a +759 snap (New Valley, Red Sea, Matruh, Giza hole) returns at -900 and the end anchor m0900 differs from the published one in about 800 Egyptian cells; the m0900-m0801 agent should override that keyframe the same way (Delta plus the Nile valley and Fayyum, the page names nothing more).

end anchor m0900: 1039 cells differ from the published anchor; about 800 are Egypt (22nd Dynasty), 21 Carchemish to Bit Adini, 6 Samaria to Israel, the rest the m1100-m1001 and m0900-m0801 patches (wey, wu, xu, assyria).

kingdom-of-israel keyframe snap at -930 (removed 5, kept by others 32) appears after events/0; no cell changes owner because of it (checked on the m0900 anchor: every Israel cell lies inside the keyframe).
the Dead Sea basin south of Judah (about 5 cells near 31.3-31.6 N, 35.4-35.6 E) stays Israel's from the united monarchy to -901; pages silent, left.
